proposals.before: Fu Qing, Labdon, Bandi, E Rong'an, Namuzhar, and San Tai
proposals.after: Fu Qing, Labdon, Bandi, Bandi's son Balu, E Rong'an, Namuzhar, and San Tai
proposals.reason: Chinese lists 班第子巴祿 after Bandi; both English fields omit Balu, Bandi's son.

proposals.before: Fu Qing, Labdon, Bandi, E Rong'an, Namuzhar, San Tai
proposals.after: Fu Qing, Labdon, Bandi, Bandi's son Balu, E Rong'an, Namuzhar, San Tai
proposals.reason: Chinese 班第子巴祿 is omitted from the literal English list.

proposals.before: Fu Qing replied in a memorial: "Under Polhané, the eldest son Gyurmé Tseten held Ali Khasha while Gyurmé Namgyal should have commanded troops at Tengri Nor, Kar Usu, and the other frontier posts.
proposals.after: Fu Qing replied in a memorial: "While Polhané lived, the eldest son Duke Gyurmé Tseten was posted at Ali Khasha, and Gyurmé Namgyal was then ordered to lead troops out to Tengri Nor, Kar Usu, and the other places.
proposals.reason: 當令 is past practice under Polhané ('was then ordered'), not English 'should have'; 公 is also omitted.

proposals.before: Fu Qing was posthumously made a first-class baron with the temple name Xianglie, and a shrine was soon ordered at Tangsikang.
proposals.after: Fu Qing was posthumously made a first-class baron with the posthumous name Xianglie, and a shrine was soon ordered at Tangsikang.
proposals.reason: 諡襄烈 is a posthumous name (谥), not a temple name (庙号). The literal English already has 'posthumous title'.

proposals.before: Under Yongzheng he followed Furdan against the Dzungars and fought at Khorgos;
proposals.after: Under Yongzheng he followed Furdan against the Dzungars and fought at Khoton Nor;
proposals.reason: 和通呼爾哈諾爾 is the 1731 Khoton Nor battle, not Khorgos (霍爾果斯).

proposals.before: In the Yongzheng reign he followed Furdan against the Dzungars and fought at Khorgos;
proposals.after: In the Yongzheng reign he followed Furdan against the Dzungars and fought at Khoton Nor;
proposals.reason: Same place-name error as the idiomatic rendering: 和通呼爾哈諾爾 is Khoton Nor, not Khorgos.

proposals.before: Labdon's clan was raised to the Bordered Yellow Banner and he received the posthumous name Zhuangguo.
proposals.after: Labdon's clan was raised to the Plain Yellow Banner and he received the posthumous name Zhuangguo.
proposals.reason: 正黃旗 is the Plain Yellow Banner; Bordered Yellow is 鑲黃旗.

proposals.before: He ordered Labdon's clan raised to the Bordered Yellow Banner, with the posthumous title Zhuangguo.
proposals.after: He ordered Labdon's clan raised to the Plain Yellow Banner, with the posthumous title Zhuangguo.
proposals.reason: 正黃旗 is Plain Yellow, not Bordered Yellow.

proposals.before: He put down the Miao revolts in Zhenqian and Yongshun within two months, and the emperor commended him.
proposals.after: He put down the Miao revolts in Zhenqian and Yongsui within two months, and the emperor commended him.
proposals.reason: 永綏 is Yongsui, not Yongshun (永順).

proposals.before: He suppressed the rebellious Miao of Zhenqian and Yongshun; within two months it was finished, and the emperor praised him.
proposals.after: He suppressed the rebellious Miao of Zhenqian and Yongsui; within two months it was finished, and the emperor praised him.
proposals.reason: 永綏 is Yongsui, not Yongshun.

proposals.before: Soon afterward he investigated Acting Sichuan Governor Jishan's report on burdensome extra levies and was ordered to serve at once as governor.
proposals.after: Soon afterward he investigated Acting Sichuan Governor Jishan's extra levies that burdened the people and was ordered to serve at once as governor.
proposals.reason: 按…加徵累民狀 is investigating Jishan's levies as an offense, not treating a report by Jishan as the source.

proposals.before: That winter he reported: "The Oirat zasag Elesen and others are grazing inside at the Burjitu River, while the Uriankhai Demchi Zhamchen is grazing inside at the headwaters of the Buyantu.
proposals.after: That winter he reported: "The Oirat jaisang Elesen and others are grazing inside at the Burjitu River, while the Uriankhai Demchi Zhamchen is grazing inside at the headwaters of the Buyantu.
proposals.reason: 宰桑 is the Oirat-Dzungar title jaisang, not Mongol zasag.

proposals.before: At E'erdélik Bandi once again sent Amursana on ahead.
proposals.after: At E'erdélik, Bandi once again sent Amursana on ahead.
proposals.reason: Missing comma fuses the place E'erdélik with the person Bandi, producing a false compound personal name.

proposals.before: Amursana asked Sebuteng Barzhur to submit a memorial for him, hoping to win overall command of the four divisions, and said he would wait for an answer until the seventh month.
proposals.after: Amursana asked that a memorial be submitted on his behalf, hoping to win overall command of the four divisions, and said he would wait for an answer until the seventh month.
proposals.reason: Chinese 乞代奏 does not name Sebuteng Barzhur in this sentence; the English invents that addressee from the previous unit.

proposals.before: He was later also honored with a portrait in the Hall of Purple Glaze.
proposals.after: He was later also honored with a portrait in the Hall of Purple Light.
proposals.reason: 紫光閣 is the Hall of Purple Light (Ziguangge), not Purple Glaze.

proposals.before: Shortly afterward he was again ordered to have his portrait placed in the Hall of Purple Glaze.
proposals.after: Shortly afterward he was again ordered to have his portrait placed in the Hall of Purple Light.
proposals.reason: 紫光閣 is the Hall of Purple Light, not Purple Glaze.

proposals.before: After the campaign he received a hereditary Cloud Cavalry Captaincy, was honored with a portrait in the Hall of Purple Glaze, and ranked first among the later fifty distinguished ministers.
proposals.after: After the campaign he received a hereditary Cloud Cavalry Captaincy, was honored with a portrait in the Hall of Purple Light, and ranked first among the later fifty distinguished ministers.
proposals.reason: 紫光閣 is the Hall of Purple Light, not Purple Glaze.

proposals.before: When the army returned he was given the hereditary office of Cloud Cavalry Captain, had his portrait placed in the Hall of Purple Glaze, and ranked first among the later fifty meritorious ministers.
proposals.after: When the army returned he was given the hereditary office of Cloud Cavalry Captain, had his portrait placed in the Hall of Purple Light, and ranked first among the later fifty meritorious ministers.
proposals.reason: 紫光閣 is the Hall of Purple Light, not Purple Glaze.

proposals.before: After further promotions he became Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent's Household in the fifth year.
proposals.after: After further promotions he became Chancellor of the Household of the Heir Apparent in the fifth year.
proposals.reason: 詹事府詹事 is chancellor of the heir apparent's household, not Grand Preceptor.

proposals.before: After further promotions, in the fifth year he was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
proposals.after: After further promotions, in the fifth year he was appointed Chancellor of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.reason: 詹事府詹事 is not Grand Preceptor.

proposals.before: Ortai tried to decline the appointment, but the emperor said: "Your late father placed E Rong'an in the Grand Council along with Zhang Tingyu's son Ruohai precisely to train them into capable officials.
proposals.after: Ortai tried to decline the appointment, but the emperor said: "E Rong'an and Zhang Tingyu's son Ruohai, as my late father ordered to serve in the Grand Council, were originally meant to be trained into capable officials.
proposals.reason: 皇考 is Qianlong's late father (Yongzheng), not Ortai's father; the literal English is already correct.

proposals.before: E Rong'an asked to be punished and argued: "The people gave from their own means, and returning the silver would only let clerks skim it off. He still asked the emperor to accept the contribution."
proposals.after: E Rong'an asked to be punished and argued: "The people gave from their own means, and returning the silver would only let clerks skim it off; I still ask that the memorial be allowed."
proposals.reason: The closing sentence is still E Rong'an's quoted plea, not narrator voice inside the quotation.

proposals.before: His portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Glaze, and the emperor himself wrote the laudatory inscription, saying: "To use him against his talents was truly my own mistake."
proposals.after: His portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Light, and the emperor himself wrote the laudatory inscription, saying: "To use him against his talents was truly my own mistake."
proposals.reason: 紫光閣 is the Hall of Purple Light, not Purple Glaze.

proposals.before: His portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Glaze; the emperor personally composed a laudatory inscription that said: "To use him against his talents was truly my mistake."
proposals.after: His portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Light; the emperor personally composed a laudatory inscription that said: "To use him against his talents was truly my mistake."
proposals.reason: 紫光閣 is the Hall of Purple Light, not Purple Glaze.

proposals.before: In the twenty-third year it was proposed that Demuqi and Shoulenge be placed in charge of routine affairs for the otok of Chadaq, chief of the surrendered Uriankhai.
proposals.after: In the twenty-third year it was proposed that demchi and shulengge officers be placed in charge of routine affairs for the otok of Chadaq, chief of the surrendered Uriankhai.
proposals.reason: 得木齊 and 收楞額 are Uriankhai official titles (demchi and shulengge), not personal names.

proposals.before: In the twenty-third year, it was proposed that for the Uriankhai surrender chief Chadaq's otok, Demuqi and Shoulenge be placed in charge of routine affairs.
proposals.after: In the twenty-third year, it was proposed that for the Uriankhai surrender chief Chadaq's otok, demchi and shulengge officers be placed in charge of routine affairs.
proposals.reason: 得木齊 and 收楞額 are official titles, not personal names.

proposals.before: He asked that Demuqi be made an assistant banner captain and Shoulenge a brave cavalry captain, with sable pelts sent yearly as tribute to Uliastai and rewarded with satin and cloth.
proposals.after: He asked that the demchi posts be converted to assistant banner captains and the shulengge posts to brave cavalry captains, with sable pelts sent yearly as tribute to Uliastai and rewarded with satin and cloth.
proposals.reason: The request converts the offices 得木齊 and 收楞額 into banner ranks, not two named men.

proposals.before: He asked that Demuqi be made an assistant banner captain, Shoulenge a brave cavalry captain; each year sable pelts would be sent as tribute to Uliastai and rewarded with satin and cloth.
proposals.after: He asked that demchi be made assistant banner captains and shulengge brave cavalry captains; each year sable pelts would be sent as tribute to Uliastai and rewarded with satin and cloth.
proposals.reason: 得木齊 and 收楞額 are offices being retitled, not individuals.

proposals.before: When Zhaohui replaced Yarhasan and led the army from Aksu toward Yarkand, Khoja Jahan surrounded him at Karakul.
proposals.after: When Zhaohui replaced Yarhasan and led the army from Aksu toward Yarkand, Khoja Jahan surrounded him at Qara Usu.
proposals.reason: 喀喇烏蘇 is the Black Water / Qara Usu near Yarkand, not the lake name Karakul.

proposals.before: When Zhaohui replaced Yarhasan and led the army from Aksu to press toward Yarkand, at Karakul he was surrounded by Khoja Jahan.
proposals.after: When Zhaohui replaced Yarhasan and led the army from Aksu to press toward Yarkand, at Qara Usu he was surrounded by Khoja Jahan.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise renders 喀喇烏蘇 as Karakul, which names the wrong place.

proposals.before: After the Muslim regions were pacified, his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Glaze.
proposals.after: After the Muslim regions were pacified, his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Light.
proposals.reason: 紫光閣 is the Hall of Purple Light, not 'Purple Glaze'.

proposals.before: Baotai rose from battalion commander to Chahar commander-in-chief and served as Tibet commissioner alongside Yamantai. When Gorkha invaded Tibet, Baotai was punished for urging the Dalai Lama and the Panchen Erdeni to flee and for concealing tribute sent before hostilities and requests brought by envoys without reporting them to the throne. The emperor changed his name to Fuxihun; he and Yamantai were stripped of office, made to wear the cangue, and Baotai was flogged four times in all.
proposals.after: Baotai rose from baitangga to Chahar commander-in-chief and served as Tibet commissioner alongside Yamantai. When Gorkha invaded Tibet, Baotai was punished for urging the Dalai Lama and the Panchen Erdeni to flee and for concealing tribute sent before hostilities and requests brought by envoys without reporting them to the throne. The emperor changed his name to Fuxihun; he and Yamantai were stripped of office, made to wear the cangue, and Baotai was flogged four times in all.
proposals.reason: 拜唐阿 is the unranked baitangga attendant post, not a battalion commander.
